# KitsuBeat

> KitsuBeat is a Japanese language learning app that teaches vocabulary and grammar through real anime songs. Users study lyrics interactively, then reinforce retention with spaced-repetition (FSRS) flashcard exercises.

## What KitsuBeat does

- Interactive lyric reader with word-by-word Japanese vocabulary breakdowns
- Spaced repetition flashcards (FSRS algorithm) for vocabulary from songs the user has studied
- Kana trainer (hiragana and katakana)
- Learning path that sequences songs by JLPT level and difficulty
- Journal with articles explaining Japanese language concepts through anime songs

## Content

KitsuBeat covers hundreds of Japanese anime songs across genres, including songs from Naruto, Attack on Titan, Fullmetal Alchemist, Demon Slayer, Bleach, One Piece, and many others. Each song includes:
- Timestamped lyrics with vocabulary annotations
- JLPT level classification (N5–N1)
- Grammar rules with explanations and example sentences
- Mnemonic memory aids for vocabulary

## Audience

Beginner to intermediate Japanese learners (JLPT N5–N3) who learn best through music and pop-culture content.

## Pages

- /songs — Browse the full song catalog
- /anime-list — Browse songs organised by anime series
- /kana — Hiragana and katakana trainer
- /path — Personalised learning path
- /journal — Articles on Japanese language through anime songs
- /review — Spaced-repetition review session

## Journal

The KitsuBeat Journal publishes articles explaining Japanese vocabulary, grammar, and cultural context using anime songs as the teaching anchor. Each article includes structured FAQ content and example sentences.

## Contact

support@kitsubeat.com

## AI Usage Disclosure

Some content on KitsuBeat (vocabulary mnemonics, kanji breakdowns, grammar explanations) is generated with AI assistance (Claude by Anthropic). All AI-generated content is reviewed and contextualised by the KitsuBeat team.
See /legal/ai-transparency for full disclosure.
